chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man: when he bows and then raises his head, should he begin and place his hands on the ground first or his knees? He said: It does not harm him whichever of the two he begins with; it is accepted from him.

His statement عليه السلام, 'It does not harm him,' means that the salat (prayer) is not invalidated for him, or that he does not deserve punishment for leaving it, because that is from the etiquettes of salat (prayer), not from its obligations for whose omission punishment is deserved.

key_terms.آدَابِ الصَّلَاةِ: the recommended etiquettes and manners of salat (prayer)
key_terms.رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ: rose up from the bowing position
key_terms.رُكْبَتَيْهِ: his two knees, as an alternative to placing the hands first
key_terms.لَا يَضُرُّهُ: it does not adversely affect him; it does not invalidate the salat (prayer)
key_terms.مَقْبُولٌ: accepted and valid in this context
key_terms.يَدَيْهِ: his two hands, placed on the ground when descending to sajdah

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, when going into sajdah, should the hands touch the ground before the knees or the knees before the hands?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that when going down for sajdah after rukuʿ, a person may place either the hands or the knees first, and the salat (prayer) remains valid either way. The report clarifies that this matter belongs to the etiquettes of salat (prayer), not its obligatory elements, so leaving one manner does not invalidate the act nor entail punishment.
